notes: Jellyfin (2026-11-03, asked for a Jellyfin adapter): the household's own media server, free and open source, with no ads, no DRM and no catalogue of anyone else's. There is no fixed address: the person types their server's address when they add Jellyfin (the catalog entry's address block; http on the home network is usual), and every page address in this adapter is written against {home}, which core fills with that address (the part before the #). Sign-in is on the page itself (the server's user cards or its form, then Remember me); no login address, the session markers decide. No ad script: the service has no ads. Everything here is a page action on the household's own server; the web client's own API object is never used (third-party-services-policy rule 3). Read live on Jellyfin's public demo, version 12.4.0 (demo.jellyfin.org/stable, the demo user), in a browser on 2026-11-03; nothing of it has run on a wall yet, so every script is to verify there.
